sections.heading: 1. HTML Document Anatomy & Boilerplate
sections.content: Every modern HTML5 document commences with '<!DOCTYPE html>', declaring the document standard to the browser. The '<html>' element encloses the entire tree, '<head>' contains page metadata, scripts, and stylesheets, while '<body>' encompasses all visual and interactive content.

sections.heading: 3. Hyperlinks & Media Elements ( and )
sections.content: The anchor element () links documents via its 'href' attribute; setting target='_blank' opens links in a new browsing context. The image element () is self-closing and mandates 'src' (asset location) and 'alt' (accessible alternative text).

definitions_and_terms.definition: Document type declaration instructing browsers to render HTML5 standard.
Hypertext Reference attribute that specifies the destination URL of a link.
Alternative text descriptor required for accessibility and fallback display.

common_pitfalls: Using multiple <h1> tags on a single page, which breaks semantic document hierarchy.
Omitting the 'alt' attribute on elements, penalizing accessibility audits.
Misconfiguring relative asset paths (e.g. failing to account for parent directory '../' syntax).
revision_checklist: Does the document declare <!DOCTYPE html> on the first line?
Is there exactly one <h1> heading defining the primary topic?
Do external anchor links include target='_blank' and rel='noopener'?
Do all elements include accurate, descriptive alt text?
